questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best riding formation?
questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Switch to a single-file line when turning, going around curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Which of these will NOT help prevent fatigue on a long ride?

options.text: Limit the distance traveled in a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: To prevent fatigue, dress to stay warm and dry. Ride no more than six hours a day and take a break every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because extreme fatigue can happen when they wear off.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol was consumed

questions.correctAnswerText: How often alcohol is consumed
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Other factors like sex, fitness level, and food intake can also matter.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle:

options.text: Should be done to avoid a hazard on a slippery road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Requires a lot of traction.
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs good traction to be safe. Do not swerve suddenly on slippery roads because your tires may lose grip.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: Which of these do you NOT need to adjust when carrying a passenger?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light position.
questions.explanation: A passenger's weight changes how the motorcycle sits. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlight, and mirrors. The brake light position does not need adjustment.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change. Pick a position that gives you the most space and helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that run parallel to the road, what should you do?

options.text: Cross the tracks at a 90-degree angle.
Avoid crossing the tracks for any reason.
Try to cross the tracks at a 45-degree angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to cross the tracks at a 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: Cross railroad tracks at a 45-degree angle or steeper. Make a quick, sharp turn. If you cross slowly or at a shallow angle, the tracks can catch your tires and cause you to lose balance.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is discouraged because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be done if the jacket is a light color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants even in hot weather. They provide safety protection and can help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: Hearing protection:

options.text: Is not necessary when wearing a full-face helmet.
Prevents you from hearing necessary road noises, such as horns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is encouraged.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing even with a helmet. Ear plugs are good hearing protection. They block harmful noise but still let you hear important sounds like car horns and sirens.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a sudden hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time and brake harder.
Do both actions at the same time, but focus mainly on swerving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: You need good tire grip to swerve safely. Do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, brake first or swerve first, then do the other action.

questions.question: When riding in a group, who should set the pace?

options.text: The rider behind the lead rider

questions.correctAnswerText: The last rider
questions.explanation: The last rider should set the pace for the group. This keeps the group together and prevents riders from becoming separated.

questions.question: If your throttle gets stuck, what should you do?

options.text: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Do not try to move the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: Try twisting the throttle back and forth several times to free it. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: If you must swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Push the handlegrip toward the direction you want to turn.
Push the handlegrip away from the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handlegrip toward the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push the handlegrip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, push the left grip, then push the right grip to straighten out. To swerve right, push the right grip, then push the left grip.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride, which action should you avoid?

options.text: Get other friends to talk them out of riding.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Keep them from drinking too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: You can prevent someone from riding while drunk by arranging other transportation, getting friends to stop them from leaving, and slowing down their drinking. Never tell them to just use quieter roads—they should not ride at all.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare to a car's stopping distance?

options.text: Cars take much longer to stop.
Cars take a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars stop in about the same distance. However, wet or slippery roads make it harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Start slowing down earlier than usual.
Keep more distance between you and other vehicles.
Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so the motorcycle responds more slowly. Ride slower, slow down earlier, and keep more distance from other vehicles. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When riding through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to see where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you turn?
questions.correctAnswerText: Just your head
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to see where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When exiting a highway in a group, what formation should riders use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation for normal group riding. Switch to single-file when going through curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Where do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips less than five miles long at speeds below 30 mph.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane is slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is usually best.

questions.question: Do you need hearing protection?

options.text: No, not if you wear a helmet.
Yes, in addition to a helmet.
No, not if you have a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, in addition to a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Hearing protection helps prevent damage while still letting you hear horns and sirens.

questions.question: When may you NOT need more following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: You need more following distance on slippery roads, in heavy traffic, or when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead. You do not need extra distance when you can see clearly through the vehicle.

questions.question: How do you achieve maximum braking?
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not lock either wheel.
questions.explanation: Use full braking pressure on both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel for maximum stopping power.
